newsitem.title: USA: General Motors readies for new walkouts - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: General Motors readies for new walkouts - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp officials are preparing for the possibility of new walkouts at plants which make transmissions and other vital parts, the Wall Street Journal said in Thursday's electronic edition.

According to people familiar with the situation, company executives are reviewing ways to build supplies and maintain production at key assembly plants if work is stopped at parts plants, the newspaper said.

General Motor's Oklahoma City car assembly plant has been on strike for nearly a month, as the United Auto Workers union wants the company to replace some of the 900 jobs cut from the plant last year when it launched production of new cars.
General Motors maintains it needs fewer workers because the cars' assembly process has been simplified.

A second strike started at a General Motors truck assembly plant in Pontiac, Mich. on April 22. U.S. automaker Chrysler Corp also faces an ongoing engine plant strike which has caused other plants to shut temporarily for parts shortages.
People close to the union were quoted in the paper as saying the UAW was not expected to target more General Motors plants until it resolved the Chrysler engine plant strike.
But according to people familiar with General Motors talks with unions, there has been little progress toward settlements, the newspaper said.
General Motors was not immediately available to comment.
